stem: A client is 8 hours postpartum after a vaginal birth and reports perineal swelling and soreness. Which comfort measure is appropriate during the first 24 hours?

options.A: Avoid local comfort measures until the swelling resolves spontaneously.
options.B: Use a warm sitz bath as the preferred first intervention immediately after birth.
options.C: Apply an ice pack for short periods to reduce swelling and pain.
options.D: Apply continuous dry heat to the perineum during the first 24 hours.

rationale: MedlinePlus postpartum guidance recommends ice packs during the first 24 hours after vaginal birth because they decrease perineal swelling and help relieve pain. Warm baths or sitz baths are generally delayed until after the first 24 hours. Therefore C is correct.
educational_objective: Use cold therapy during the first 24 hours after vaginal birth to reduce perineal swelling and discomfort; warm baths are introduced after that early period.
source_document_title: After vaginal delivery - in the hospital
source_locator: Care of the Vagina and Perineum — ice packs in the first 24 hours decrease swelling and pain; warm baths after 24 hours.
source_claim_supported: Perineal ice packs are appropriate during the first 24 hours postpartum to reduce swelling and pain; warm baths are delayed until after 24 hours.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity → Basic Care and Comfort; nonpharmacologic comfort measures and postpartum care activities.
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — early postpartum perineal comfort

correction_summary: Clinical content and answer were retained. The source URL was corrected from the discharge page to the MedlinePlus in-hospital postpartum page that contains the exact first-24-hour ice-pack and post-24-hour warm-bath guidance.

audit_findings.source_authority: NLM MedlinePlus is an appropriate authoritative patient-care reference for this basic-care instruction.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Care of the Vagina and Perineum directly states the first-24-hour cold therapy and delayed warm baths.
audit_findings.claim_audit: The item uses only the directly supported 24-hour distinction; no unsupported duration for ice application was specified beyond short periods.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because active comfort care is recommended.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because warm bath/sitz bath is delayed until after 24 hours.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because continuous dry heat is not the recommended early measure.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: At 8 hours postpartum, only C matches the cited timing guidance.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are local comfort strategies of similar structure.
audit_findings.blueprint: Fits Basic Care and Comfort through nonpharmacologic postpartum comfort care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Second-pass review verified the exact 24-hour timing and corrected the source page mismatch; no second answer remains.
